solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Left on light to show

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Instructions for a stage lamp left switched on to illuminate a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the charade signal: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict or represent it, a synonym of show.

clue.text: Turn, retreating from shots

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for shots is read from its end

parts.note: nips are small drinks of spirits, shots

explanation.surface: A soldier turning and falling back from gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns NIPS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a turn or rotation, synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Stand at waterfront to see animal

indicators.note: the stand is placed at, that is beside and after, the first piece

parts.note: the front of the word water is its first letter, W
an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: Someone sets up by the harbour to watch some wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: The weasel is a small carnivorous mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Is left in its case for her

indicators.note: the first words form a case or casing holding the next word inside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something left inside its box for a woman to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is left' looks like a passive aside but is the definition, the verb's sense of receiving a bequest; 'case for' wraps the first two words round the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is left property in a will receives it as an inheritance, the verb's sense.

clue.text: Tell in writing to give waiter good tip

definitions.meaning: to pass on a message on paper for someone
to hand over a banknote as a generous gratuity

explanation.surface: Advice on letting a waiter know your thoughts, or rewarding him well.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is both a written message and a banknote, so the phrase fits both senses.

clue.text: Having been terribly healthy gives advantage

indicators.note: used as an anagram signal: the letters of the word are mangled badly

parts.note: fit means in good health

explanation.surface: Good health is a head start in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage, synonymous nouns.

clue.text: It rhymes with 'two-time'

parts.note: a couple is a pair, two

explanation.surface: A wordplay quip that something chimes with being unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-time' looks like the verb meaning cheat on a partner, but it splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines of verse, so it is something that rhymes.

clue.text: Wound up being compromised no end

indicators.note: signals that the named word is taken away, the word is lost

parts.note: something endangered is at risk, compromised
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone irritated at being let down in a deal that collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' sounds like 'very much' but tells you to remove END from ENDANGERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wound up is to be irritated, made cross, the same as made furious.

clue.text: It needs a good blow to drive it home

definitions.text: It needs a good blow to drive it home

parts.words: It needs a good blow to drive it home
parts.note: a strong wind propels a craft under canvas back to port, like a hammer blow driving a nail

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel with canvas depends on wind to carry it to harbour, its home port.

clue.text: Very embarrassed look?

parts.note: financially embarrassed means short of money, and the very worst case is stony broke, so the look is a stony one

explanation.definitionFit: A cold, fixed gaze, cryptically the expression of someone stony broke.

clue.text: Concept of life, according to Monsieur, taken by women

indicators.note: the French word is taken along by the abbreviation, sitting next to it

parts.note: vie is the French word for life

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's philosophy of life, as received by women.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is an opinion or idea, a near synonym of concept.

clue.text: In paler ensemble, everything matching

indicators.note: the word for everything goes inside the regrouped letters
an ensemble puts things together in a new arrangement, so the letters are regrouped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A fashion note: everything matches in an outfit of paler shades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensemble' rearranges the first word to PAREL; 'In' splits that after its third letter to hold the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines or cases correspond exactly, matching each other.

clue.text: However perfectly matched

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both nevertheless and completely identical.

clue.text: Right-leaning political grouping losing short election

indicators.note: the letters of the word are grouped into a new order
signals that some letters are dropped from that pool before rearranging
shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a poll is an election, a vote

explanation.surface: A conservative party coalition that has just lost a snap election.
explanation.walkthrough: Take POL from POLITICAL and 'grouping' rearranges the remaining ITICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, a witty twist on a political leaning.

clue.text: With 'Drat! An express train!' get angry

parts.note: blow is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like drat
a fast service making only a single halt

explanation.surface: A frustrated commuter swearing as a fast train thunders through the station.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper, to become furious.

clue.text: Had altercation, somehow managed to get run in

indicators.note: the abbreviation is put inside the other word

parts.note: to wangle something is to obtain it by cunning
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone argued, then contrived to get a car run in.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to argue or quarrel noisily, to have an altercation.

clue.text: Separate. Is love dead?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
late means deceased

explanation.surface: A sad question after a breakup: are we apart, has romance died?
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart, separate, as verbs.

clue.text: Ran to catch, also crouching

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside, as if catching it

parts.note: sped means ran fast
too means also

explanation.surface: A fielder racing to take a catch, bending low too.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooped describes a body bent forward and down, much like crouching.

clue.text: Note maths error, making complaint

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: a mistake, so the letters of the word are jumbled wrongly

explanation.surface: A teacher spotting a sum gone wrong, prompting a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an illness; this breathing disorder is an example.

clue.text: Hence rent, or let out, in an Italian resort

parts.note: so means therefore, hence

indicators.note: the letters are released and reassembled freely

explanation.surface: Advice on paying rent or subletting a holiday flat in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Bay of Naples is a well-known holiday destination in Italy.

clue.text: Furious kid has been allowed to imbibe spirit

indicators.note: the first word drinks in the spirit, holding it inside

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease, kid them
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A parent livid that their child was allowed alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging means extremely angry, a synonym of furious.

clue.text: Regrettably, I entered with false name

indicators.note: the answer with the letter I entered into it gives the false name, so that letter comes out of it here

parts.note: an alias is an assumed name

explanation.surface: A confession: sadly I checked in under an assumed name.
explanation.walkthrough: A reversed instruction: the answer plus an entered I makes ALIAS, so ALIAS minus I is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses sorrow or regret, like unfortunately.

clue.text: Gun aimed, not as good as one used to be

definitions.meaning: a gun pointed at something is about to shoot, and pot means shoot game

definitions.text: not as good as one used to be

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deteriorating, and literally reads as about to shoot.

clue.text: Dear me, I've slipped up, duplicating a nought on the addition

indicators.note: doubling the piece so it appears twice

parts.note: nought is zero, the letter O
PS, postscript, is an addition to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for writing an extra zero on a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what one says on making a small mistake.

clue.text: Puzzled out

definitions.meaning: dismissed in cricket when the wicket-keeper breaks the wicket with the batsman out of his ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means baffled, and in cricket a batsman dismissed this way is out.

clue.text: Scrap cut to give to dog?

parts.note: snip means cut
to pet is to stroke affectionately, what one gives a dog

explanation.surface: Offering the dog a trimmed leftover from the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece, a scrap or fragment.
